Issued at 409 AM CDT Sat Jul 25 2026

Heat Building Today & Storm Potential: 

A warmer and moisture laden airmass has begun to push into the 
region overnight, a result of a slight eastward progression to 
the fairly pronounced upper-level ridge into the region. 
Consequently, expecting temperatures to respond accordingly with
mean apparent temperatures in the NBM reaching around 100 
degrees for portions of southeast MN where a Heat Advisory 
remains in effect. In addition to the heat, there are some low- 
end potential for isolated storms generally near and north of 
I-90 in Wisconsin where the thermal ridge is less prevalent and 
daytime heating may allow for the capping inversion, that 
resulted from the aforementioned warm advection, to break. If 
convection can manifest late this afternoon and into the 
evening, very favorable shear profiles noted by the elongated 
mid-level hodographs would suggest any isolated storms could 
trend supercellular, especially with around 2000-2500 J/kg of 
MUCAPE to work with. In this environment, large hail and 
damaging wind gusts would be possible with the aforementioned 
shear and instability accompanied with relatively steep low- 
level lapse rates and impressive DCAPE values to around 1500 
J/kg due to a profound dry layer between 500-700mb (which may 
work to inhibit convection as well). 

Heat & Storm Potential Increasing Sunday:

Continued south to southwesterly surface flow will continue to 
push a warmer airmass into the region through the weekend. As a
result, there are high probabilities (60-80%) in the grand 
ensemble (GEFS/EC/Canadian ensemble) for heat indices to exceed 
100 degrees with even some spots seeing heat indices nearing 105
degrees for Sunday. Given the confidence and in collaboration
with neighboring forecast offices, have converted Extreme Heat
Watch to an Extreme Heat Warning. The one caveat to this will 
be exactly how convection evolves on Sunday as this ridge
nears...

Overall, convective evolution on Sunday appears fairly low 
confidence with pronounced capping in place across many of the 
model soundings and uncertainty on when various shortwave 
perturbations would traverse the area. The main concern comes 
later into the afternoon and evening as more favorable 500mb 
flow moves into northern WI with stronger forcing for ascent, 
however there remains uncertainty on how far east the ridge has 
progressed. There remains a very possible scenario that the 
ridge has pushed too far east through the local area that much 
of the evening convection would keep north and east of the area,
however there are just as many solutions that would keep 
convection in play across the local area. In this scenario, an 
MCS trekking through the local area with a damaging wind gust 
risk would be of highest concern. Overall, it's inherently an inversely
proportional relationship: if the ridge pushes further east, 
the confidence for dangerous heat indices (105F or greater) 
increases further and storm chances decrease; if the ridge 
struggles to push east, confidence for storms increases and 
dangerous heat decreases. 

Heat Confidence Decreases Into Monday:

By the time Monday rolls around, the upper-level ridge hardly shifts 
much keeping our region in southwesterly surface flow to start the 
day on Monday. Consequently, expecting highs to yet again reach into 
the 90s for much of the local area with heat indices approaching 100 
to 105 degrees south of I-90. As we head later into the day on 
Monday, guidance generally agrees on pushing a weak front 
through the area during the afternoon and evening. While 
confidence is fairly low (under 15% chance) for anything to 
develop along this front on Monday afternoon and evening at this
point due to the lack of convergence along it and a pronounce 
dry layer in model soundings aloft, there remains respectable 
instability and shear in place in the event thermal profiles do 
become uncapped and forcing trends more favorably for 
convection. Have continued the previous Extreme Heat Watch
Sunday night through Monday in collaboration with neighboring
forecast offices given current apparent temperature forecasts 
only flirting near Warning criteria on Monday.

All said, confidence is fairly high for impactful heat through 
Monday with some questions how any convection many affect 
temperatures over this period. Convective trends are a bit lower 
confidence due to the ridge and its resultant capping not clearly 
defined across the area in model guidance. Shear profiles seem 
consistently sufficient for the development for severe storms during 
this period with elongated hodographs from a strong and persistent 
250-500mb jet streak. But again, whether these can be utilized are 
heavily dependent on how much the ridge builds into the region.
